# Covariant class siblings

Run `test_mobile_android_original_raw_parameters.py --dependency-interface
--abstract-dependency-parent --plain-class-covariance --covariant-siblings`.
The original public/protected implementation methods each retain two bridges,
one for each nominal ancestor return slot. Before freezing the owned input, the runner removes the two middle-class
compiler entries while preserving every other body, descriptor and constant.
This models an abstract middle declaration without broader bridges. The SDK
then remains immutable; both concrete child bridges stay present.

The native matrix includes checked and unchecked return adapters, explicit
and absent class Signatures, linked and direct paths, reversed classes and
methods, and a middle abstract ancestor without a broader bridge. Missing
original receipts, non-bridges, invalid flags, casts, argument flow, different
targets, final ancestors and unknown result ancestry fail.

The immutable wrapper checks eight reflected and method-handle routes on an
original receiver and independent subclass: 48 additional values, 112
identities, 64 state observations and 24 ordered failures. Complete runtime
inventory and class/member metadata recompile unchanged. All four original
input bridges remain disclosed as source projections. Same-Code role and
visibility mutations fail without producing a recovery directory.

Eight input classes and twenty-four original methods retain complete metadata
and runtime inventory; the unchanged dependency contributes no recovered copies.
